governance_rules.name: New Orchestrators MUST Use Scaffolder
governance_rules.description:
ALL NEW orchestrators MUST be created via the Orchestrator Scaffolder
(`src/tools/orchestrator_scaffolder.py`). This ensures:
1. MasterOrchestrator registration (@register_with_master decorator)
2. 4-tier governance compliance injection
3. Manifest contract validation
4. Test stub generation
5. Team ownership tracking

EXCEPTION: Legacy orchestrators created before this rule may remain
non-compliant until formal migration (AC-MIGRATE-001 in Phase 5).

CRITICAL: MasterOrchestrator is IN CHARGE - never bypassed.

legacy_orchestrators.description: Orchestrators created before CORE-021 are exempt until AC-MIGRATE-001

future_work.description: Migrate legacy orchestrators to scaffolder compliance

fail: New orchestrator without manifest in cortex-brain/manifests/

governance_rules.name: Kebab-Case File Naming with 20-Character Limit
governance_rules.description:
ALL file names MUST follow kebab-case format (lowercase, hyphen-separated)
with a maximum of 20 characters EXCLUDING the file extension.

This rule is FINAL and SUPERSEDES any conflicting naming conventions
elsewhere in the codebase or documentation.

Format: `{name}.{ext}` where:
- `name` = 1-20 lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens
- Hyphens cannot be leading, trailing, or consecutive
- Extension is NOT counted in the 20-character limit

EXCEPTIONS (grandfathered):
- Python files with underscores in src/ (Python module convention)
- __init__.py, __main__.py, conftest.py (Python special files)
- LICENSE, README.md, Makefile (standard project files)
- .gitignore, .env, .editorconfig (dotfiles)
validation: No uppercase characters in file name
No underscores in file name (except Python src/ files)

python_modules.description: Python files in src/ may use underscores per PEP 8

supersedes.description: This rule is FINAL and overrides any conflicting rules

migration_guidance.description: Existing files violating this rule should be renamed

governance_rules.rationale:
Kebab-case with length limits ensures:
1. Cross-platform compatibility (Windows, macOS, Linux)
2. URL-safe file names (no encoding needed)
3. Readable file names (hyphens more readable than underscores)
4. Consistent naming across entire codebase
5. Predictable file discovery and sorting
6. Git-friendly (avoids case-sensitivity issues)
7. Terminal-friendly (no quoting needed)
8. 20-char limit prevents unwieldy names while allowing descriptive names

governance_rules.name: File Type-Specific Validation Required Before Commit
governance_rules.description:
Modified files MUST pass file-type-specific validation before state
changes (git commit, plan completion, orchestrator finish).

This is a PRE-COMMIT quality gate, NOT a TDD cycle requirement.
Validation happens once at completion, not during development iterations.

Validation per file type:
- .html → HTML5 syntax (html5lib) + WCAG AA compliance (zero tolerance)
- .yaml → Schema validation + YAML syntax (already enforced by OE-002)
- .py → pytest + test coverage (handled by TDD-Master via CORE-019)
- .json → JSON syntax validation
- .css → CSS syntax validation (optional)

CRITICAL: HTML files MUST NOT be left in broken states. Any HTML
modification by any orchestrator or GitHub Copilot MUST result in
valid HTML5 with zero parse errors.

html_files: Parse with html5lib (TreeBuilder with strict mode)
No unclosed tags, no malformed attributes
WCAG AA compliance (contrast ratios, semantic HTML, ARIA)
python_files: All tests pass (TDD-Master ensures this via CORE-019)
No validation needed at pre-commit (already tested)
json_files: Schema validation if JSON schema exists

applies_to: Manual HTML edits by GitHub Copilot

on_html_validation_failure.message:
❌ HTML VALIDATION FAILED

Modified HTML file(s) contain syntax errors or WCAG violations.
All HTML must be valid HTML5 with zero parse errors.

Run validator manually:
  python -m src.orchestrators.html_view.validators.html_validator <file.html>

Or fix via HTMLViewOrchestrator:
  python -m src.main "fix visual issues in <file.html>"

pass: Modified docs/features/index.html → html5lib validates → ✓ commit allowed
Fixed docs/orchestrators/planning.html → WCAG AA compliant → ✓ commit allowed
Updated config.yaml → schema valid → ✓ commit allowed (OE-002)
fail: Modified index.html with unclosed <div> → ❌ blocked (HTML5 error)
Added feature.html with contrast ratio 2.5:1 → ❌ blocked (WCAG AA requires 4.5:1)

integration_points: HTMLViewOrchestrator Phase 5 (VALIDATION) runs same checks during development
Pre-commit hook (scripts/pre-commit) enforces at commit time
GitHub Copilot edits HTML → pre-commit catches issues before merge
TDD-Master does NOT validate HTML (separation of concerns)
performance: Validation only on modified files (not entire codebase)
WCAG validation: ~200ms per file (contrast checks, semantic analysis)
Total overhead: <1 second for typical commits (1-5 HTML files)
governance_rules.rationale:
Zero-tolerance HTML validation prevents:
1. Broken HTML merged into main branch (blocks GitHubPages deployment)
2. WCAG AA violations (accessibility compliance failures)
3. Browser rendering issues (parse errors cause layout breaks)
4. Developer confusion (debug time wasted on malformed HTML)
5. Accumulated technical debt (broken HTML compounds over time)

This rule addresses the observed pattern of TDD-Master and other
orchestrators leaving HTML in broken states. By validating at the
quality gate layer (pre-commit), we catch issues before they pollute
the repository.

Architectural rationale:
- HTML validation is NOT a TDD concern (HTML is declarative, not testable code)
- Separation of concerns: HTMLViewOrchestrator handles HTML, TDD-Master handles code
- Pre-commit hooks are the correct architectural layer for cross-cutting quality checks
- This approach is extensible (easy to add CSS linting, Markdown validation, etc.)
